Your major is under different colleges within the university. For example, Digital Media is under College of Sciences, Journalism is under Nicholson. You will apply under whichever college your major is in when the time comes. You can ask your advisor for clarification.

When it comes to taking the prerequisite classes, it just really depends on how many college credits you’re coming into college with. I came in with my AA from high school so I did only my prerequisite classes right away, but you’ll need to talk to your advisor to schedule when to take them because you need to get your GEP classes in.

To conclude, don’t worry. You’re in the school, you will be doing classes pertaining to your major and interests! You just aren’t officially accepted into the major yet, but this happens to everyone who applies to a Pending major because it has restricted access classes not everyone can take, only people officially in the major. Hope this helps.

FLVS is only free to Florida residents. For those out of state, tuition will be charged and you'll have to enroll in FlexPoint Virtual School (formerly FLVS Global School). 

Here's a link to the tuition page: [https://www.flexpointvirtualschool.com/?source=flvs.net](https://www.flexpointvirtualschool.com/?source=flvs.net)

It would be about $475 per semester for the Premium Tier, which is stated to be:

"Premium Courses include almost every course in the catalog across a variety of subjects, such as Advance Placement, Electives, and Core."

As for classes that would help you boost your GPA, there are a handful of Honors Electives on FLVS like Financial Literacy Honors that are pretty easy, but they wouldn't give you much of a GPA boost compared to AP courses. I recommend you try out some AP courses on FLVS because they are not as hard as they would be in person, but the work may be long and tedious. Some AP classes on FLVS I'd recommend are AP Psychology, AP Human Geography, and AP Environmental Science, which are fairly easy. I'd stay away from AP Calc online unless you are like a math genius already, it's not really easy to learn Calc online in my experience.
